_meta.scope: L2 encoding scales — every ordered/nominal color scale found in Piru/Shared/PiruWidget/PiruLiveActivityExtension. Values are extracted verbatim from source, not computed. Oklch/contrast math is intentionally NOT performed here.
_meta.value_encoding: each step's light/dark value is one of: {"hex": "RRGGBB"} (from Color(hex:)), {"rgb": [r,g,b]} (0..1 floats from Color(red:green:blue:) or UIColor(red:...), sRGB per ColorHex.swift/native init), {"system": "name"} (a bare SwiftUI/UIKit dynamic system color, e.g. ".orange" — its actual light/dark pixel values are Apple's, not captured here), or {"opacity_of": "<ref>", "alpha": N} for a tint applied to another scale's value.

scales.name: Route of administration tint
scales.note: The one scale in the app with explicit, separately-tuned light/dark hex pairs per step, documented rationale (Route:69-68): 'as ~11pt text on a near-white card several hues fail small-text contrast (orange/green worst), so light mode darkens each toward >=4.5:1'. Reference case for what every other scale below should look like.

scales.name: Dose level (Sub-threshold -> Heavy)
scales.source: Piru/Domain/Substance.swift:171-188 (DoseLevel enum + STRING color field, likely dead); Piru/Views/Components/DoseLevelIndicator.swift:167-186 (swiftUIColor + labelColor)
scales.note: THREE independent encodings of the same 6-step scale coexist. (1) Substance.swift:179 DoseLevel.color returns a raw STRING ("gray"/"blue"/.../"red") -- grep found ZERO consumers anywhere in Piru/Shared outside its own declaration; likely dead code, flagging rather than asserting. (2) DoseLevelIndicator.swift:167-177 swiftUIColor -- the fill/dot color, bare SwiftUI system colors, single value for both appearances (relies on system dynamism, no custom light/dark tuning). (3) DoseLevelIndicator.swift:183-186 labelColor -- 'legible text variant': identical to swiftUIColor for 5 of 6 steps, but .common swaps to Theme.legibleYellow (a real light/dark-tuned pair, Theme.swift:12-16) instead of bare system .yellow.

steps.note: the ONLY step where swiftUIColor != labelColor

consumers.role: dot + text (BUG: uses swiftUIColor, not labelColor)

consumers.note: not colored by the scale (Theme.secondaryLabel) but <13pt text sitting directly on scale-colored segments

scales.flag: CONTRAST BUG CANDIDATE: DoseLevelIndicator.swift:21-23's own level-name text uses swiftUIColor (bare system .yellow for 'Common'), not labelColor -- every OTHER one of the 10 consumers listed above correctly uses labelColor's legible amber-in-light swap. This is the ladder header on the Edit-dose screens (via DoseInfoView, EntryFormView.swift:264 / EntryEditContent.swift:136) -- 'Common' would render pure system yellow subheadline-semibold text on a near-white card in light mode, the exact failure Theme.legibleYellow's doc comment says it exists to prevent.

scales.name: Experience phase -- hex-ramp definition
scales.cardinality: ordered (temporal/narrative arc, NOT a magnitude ramp)
scales.source: Piru/Utilities/SessionReportPDF.swift:10-14; Piru/Views/Components/DosePhaseProgressBar.swift:24-28; Shared/TimelineGraphView.swift:1942-1945 (only 4 of 5 phases wired here -- see note)
scales.note: SessionReportPDF.swift:8 comment: 'matches DosePhaseProgressBar so the export reads like the app' -- these two are a CONFIRMED-INTENTIONAL shared ramp, not drift. TimelineGraphView.swift:1942-1945 wires the same 4 hex literals (onset/comeup/peak/offset) as background bands (:1975, band.color.opacity(0.12)) but its excerpt did not show a 5th 'after' band being constructed at those lines -- worth the colorimetry pass double-checking TimelineGraphView for an afterglow band elsewhere before assuming it's missing. Values are a single hex per step, no separate dark-mode tuning (relies on Color(hex:) being scheme-agnostic sRGB -- see asset-catalog-migration.md).

steps.note: identical to onset -- deliberate: an arc that returns to its starting gray, not a 5-distinct-hue ramp

scales.name: Experience phase -- DoseLevelIndicator.ExperiencePhase definition (CONFLICTS with experience_phase_hex_ramp)
scales.cardinality: ordered (temporal/narrative arc, NOT a magnitude ramp)
screens: Substance detail 'Duration' card (DoseInfoView.swift:261-277, via DoseInfoView call sites EntryFormView.swift:264 / EntryEditContent.swift:136)
DurationTimelineBar / DurationPhaseRows (Piru/Views/Components/DurationViews.swift), consumed by the same Edit-flow files
scales.note: CONFIRMED CONFLICT with experience_phase_hex_ramp: same 5 phase names, completely different hue assignment (peak is green in one, orange in the other; comeup is blue in one, teal in the other). Both scales' consumers trace back to the SAME dose entry going through Edit (this scale) vs Read (the hex ramp) -- a user editing a dose then viewing it sees 'peak' flip from orange to green. Not literally simultaneous on one screen, but back-to-back in one user flow, which is arguably more noticeable than a static duplicate.

consumers.font: not captured -- row helper, re-check at implementation time

consumers.role: duration block row label (uncolored text, color used elsewhere in row)

scales.name: Interaction severity
scales.note: color and labelColor are IDENTICAL for 2 of 3 steps (unsafe, dangerous); only caution swaps bare .yellow for Theme.legibleYellow via labelColor. Confirmed 3 real call sites STILL use the unswapped raw .color for text at <13-15pt sizes -- see flags below.

flags_raw_color_used_for_text.severity: HIGH -- caption (smallest common text size) + bold + uppercase + raw system yellow on a themeCard() surface when top result is .caution
MEDIUM -- subheadline is larger than caption but still raw yellow-on-card for .caution

flags_raw_color_used_for_text.text: not yet confirmed as text vs. icon-only -- flagged for re-check, lower confidence than the two above

scales.name: Adherence status
scales.cardinality: nominal (complete/partial/missed are a quality order; noData is out-of-band)
scales.source: Piru/Views/Insights/AdherenceView.swift -- hand-declared 3 independent times in one file
scales.note: Same finding as component-sameness.md#F6, restated here as raw color values. All three declarations agree on hue-per-case but differ on exact icon glyph AND none share one enum extension.

declarations.role: calendar-cell dot fill (0.1 opacity) + bare glyph (checkmark/circle.lefthalf.filled/xmark/blank), size 8
declarations.font: .system(size: 8, weight: .bold) for checkmark/xmark; .system(size: 8) for the half-circle

declarations.role: icon + text, NO capsule/fill background at all (plain HStack)
declarations.icons: checkmark.circle.fill / circle.lefthalf.filled / xmark.circle.fill / minus.circle (circle-composited, differs from the calendar cell's bare glyphs)

declarations.site: monthly adherence-rate percentage (NOT keyed off the AdherenceStatus enum at all -- a separately invented threshold)
declarations.thresholds: rate >= 0.8 -> green, rate >= 0.5 -> orange, else red

scales.name: Dose tier strip (in-app ladder disclosure)
scales.role: growing filled Circle, diameters [7,10,13,15,18]; text below each disc is Theme.secondaryLabel/primary, NOT scale-colored
scales.note: One of (at least) 3 distinct dose-intensity color scales in the app -- see dose_level and dose_intensity_dial. 5 steps here (no 'Sub-threshold', no 'Overdose'), vs. dose_level's 6 and dose_intensity_dial's 6. Compare hues at each position: this scale's position 1 (Light) = pure green 34C759 while dose_level's position 2 (Light) = system .green and dose_intensity_dial's position 1 (Light) = 8ED04A (yellow-green) -- three different greens for 'Light' dose.

scales.name: Dose intensity dial (drug.community spectrum, Effects & Intensity screen)
scales.role: circular arc gauge fill (see IntensityGauge, :195+) + band-name readout text
scales.note: Third distinct dose-intensity scale (see dose_level, dose_tier_strip). 6 steps, labels Threshold/Light/Common/Strong/Heavy/Overdose -- the only one of the three with an explicit top-end 'Overdose' label, and the only one with 6 smoothly-interpolated stops rather than named system colors.

scales.name: Inventory stock status
scales.cardinality: ordered (ok < low < out in attention priority, per sortIndex)
scales.note: Deliberately NOT a green/red ramp -- code comment (:5-7) states the house rule explicitly: 'color carries meaning only for Low/Out; a healthy supply reads neutral.' numberColor and barTint are identical across both roles here (unusual among these scales -- most have a text/fill split).

related_but_distinct.note: A SEPARATE bar-tint path exists for the same InventoryItem: InventoryItem.supplyBarTint (InventorySupport.swift:74-80) uses the substance's OWN identity color (L3, opacity 0.5) instead of StockStatus.barTint -- this is DIV-031 in divergences.md, restated here as a scale-vs-identity-color collision: two different color systems (L2 status vs L3 identity) both claim the same 'inventory bar fill' role at different call sites (SubstanceCardView.swift:175 and InventoryStockSection.swift:81 use barTint; InventorySupport.swift:74-80's supplyBarTint is the substance-color path).

scales.name: Tolerance bar bands (tachyphylaxis/tolerance/deep)
scales.cardinality: NOT a semantic color scale -- alpha-ordered steps of ONE identity color
scales.note: IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the brief's expectation: this is not a 5th green-red severity ramp. Each band is the SAME receptor-family identity color (familyColor, an L3-style per-mechanism hue) at three fixed alphas: 0.5 (Tachyphylaxis, fastest/shallowest), 0.82 (Tolerance), 1.0/opaque (Deep, slowest/deepest). Ordered fast-to-slow, encoded as light-to-dark of one hue rather than a hue ramp. ToleranceBucket (ToleranceRow.swift:257-285, 5 cases rested/mild/moderate/high/veryHigh) supplies WORDS only (no .color property found) -- the gauge's visible color always comes from familyColor, not from the bucket.

value.ref: familyColor (per-receptor-class identity, L3, not enumerated here)

scales.name: Substance category (Library taxonomy)
scales.note: 29 cases, no ordering. IMPORTANT: 9 of 29 use a plain Color(red:green:blue:) literal with ZERO light/dark tuning (same pixel both appearances) -- dysdelic, deliriant, ampakine, eugeroic, depressant, orexinAntagonist, antihistamine, peptide, anticonvulsant. The other 20 use bare system color names (.orange, .purple, .cyan, etc., some with .opacity()) which DO get free system-level light/dark adaptation from UIKit, but that adaptation is Apple's default curve, not anything Piru tuned -- unlike route_tint's deliberately hand-tuned pairs.

scales.name: Chart structural chrome (gridlines, axis text, fill-under-curve, now-line) -- NOT per-substance identity, which is L3 and out of scope here
scales.cardinality: n/a -- a fixed alpha vocabulary layered under whichever L3 identity color a curve uses

entries.flag: TEXT-BEARING AT 10pt -- smallest text-bearing scale entry found in the whole audit

l1_overlap_candidates: dose_level.common and interaction_severity.caution both terminate on the SAME two-value pair (system .yellow / Theme.legibleYellow) -- confirmed shared reference, not just coincidental hue match.

adherence_status.missed, interaction_severity.dangerous, stock_status.out, and substance_category.opioid all use bare system .red -- likely fine (red-for-danger is a defensible universal), but confirm none of these collide with a would-be semantic/danger asset-catalog token in a way that changes look intent.
non_monotonic_lightness_candidates_eyeba: dose_level.swiftUIColor (gray/blue/green/yellow/orange/red): yellow at position 3 of 6 reads as the single brightest step sandwiched between darker neighbors -- classic non-monotonic shape, needs your Oklab L pass to confirm.

experience_phase_hex_ramp and experience_phase_system_ramp are BOTH deliberately non-monotonic by design (narrative arc returning toward a neutral start/end, not a magnitude ramp) -- do not flag these as broken; the 'defect' would be treating them as ordinal-intensity scales.

dose_tier_strip and dose_intensity_dial both read as plausible monotonic decreasing-L ramps on eyeball, but the 'Light' step differs in exact green across all three dose-intensity scales (pure #34C759 vs #8ED04A vs system .green) -- worth checking whether they're at least monotonically consistent with each other, not just internally.
light_dark_mismatch: substance_category: 9 of 29 cases (dysdelic, deliriant, ampakine, eugeroic, depressant, orexinAntagonist, antihistamine, peptide, anticonvulsant) are plain Color(red:) literals with NO dark-mode variant at all -- same pixel both appearances, unlike route_tint's fully-tuned pairs.

dose_level.swiftUIColor: every step is a bare system color name (single declaration, relies on iOS's own light/dark dynamism) EXCEPT .common's labelColor variant, which is the only step with an explicit, Piru-authored light/dark pair (Theme.legibleYellow) -- an inconsistent one-off inside an otherwise-uniform scale.

experience_phase_hex_ramp and dose_tier_strip / dose_intensity_dial: all Color(hex:) literals, meaning (per asset-catalog-migration.md) they are unambiguously sRGB with zero appearance-based variation today -- every step in these three scales is a single fixed value for both light and dark.
